Manage webhooks

:::tip[Learn more]
The Bronto docs explain the platform concept behind this command: [docs.bronto.io/integrations/webhooks](https://docs.bronto.io/integrations/webhooks)
:::

```sh
bronto webhooks <command> [flags]
```

#### Subcommands

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`bronto webhooks create`](/reference/commands/webhooks/#bronto-webhooks-create) | Create a webhook |
| [`bronto webhooks delete`](/reference/commands/webhooks/#bronto-webhooks-delete) | Delete a webhook |
| [`bronto webhooks list`](/reference/commands/webhooks/#bronto-webhooks-list) | List webhooks |
| [`bronto webhooks update`](/reference/commands/webhooks/#bronto-webhooks-update) | Update a webhook |

Also accepts the [global flags](/reference/commands/global-flags/).

## bronto webhooks create

Create a webhook

```sh
bronto webhooks create [flags]
```

#### Flags

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--field` | `-f` | stringArray |  | request body field as key=value; values parse as JSON when possible (repeatable) |
| `--input` |  | string |  | read the request body from a file, or - for stdin |

Also accepts the [global flags](/reference/commands/global-flags/).

#### Examples

```sh
bronto webhooks create -f name=<name> -f url=<url>
bronto webhooks create --input body.json
```
